speaker: Mikel Arteta
quote_text:
If you have a question, raise your hand.  I think we've got Mike here as well,  
so we'll kick off with Tom from Football London.  Hi, Mikel. Point apiece. Is that a fair reflection  
of the performance? I think we deserve more, but  that's what we got at the end, a really tough  
place to come. What they do, they do it really  well, constantly putting the balls. There's no  
balls into the last line, dealing with direct play  and second actions. I think we haven't conceded  
anything in the game, which was really positive.  We were one-nil up, have some big opportunities,  
run into spaces. We didn't finalise the action.  Second half, we started good, start to dominate  
the game, they're going to be more aggressive,  we'll have more spaces. We did the opposite,  
we give the bonus straight to the keeper, direct  play, trouble, again, direct play, and the referee  
decides to give a penalty. That changes the course  of the game, which I'm here to give my opinion,  
and after seeing it 15 times, there is no way  that, in my opinion, that's a penalty. Because if  
there is, then O'Brien has to be out and Everton  has to play with 10 men. That's clear. And after  
that, again, dominated the game, really not get  too much momentum because he's constantly breaking  
the play and a big part of that was down to all  because after that, I play, we get very cheap  
prefigures away. But yeah, we have two big chances  to win the game. We didn't convert them. So we  
have to accept the point. I feel like we've spoken  a lot after games where refereeing decisions have  
come up this season and obviously the gap between  yourselves and Liverpool is quite significant. Do  
you feel as though that has played into maybe why  the gap is so large this season? I'm married to  
Liverpool, the way they are winning their football  matches and talking a reflection of what happened  
today, what was really relevant for their score.  And there's no question that apart from that they  
had nothing. But obviously that changes completely  the momentum and the results. Hi, Mikel. It's been  
a few times now with Myles Lewis-Skelly in certain  situations in defensive scenarios where there's  
been controversy. Do you think in some ways  he's been targeted by referees because he's been  
involved in these situations in the past? No, I  don't think any referee targets have played. Sam,  
I'm sure we need more. Hello, Mikel. Just in the  team you picked, obviously a lot of first teamers  
all left out and then they came on the end.  Presumably that's all with Real Madrid in mind,  
is it? Well, there were four players, they could  not start the game after what happened with  
Fulham. And we always lead the injury of Gabriel,  so that forces you as well to make some changes  
and as well because players deserve to play  minutes. So I'm very happy with that. I mean,  
everybody has to be important, has to feel  important. They have so many games coming up  
right now and I will have to rely on all of them.  Just so sorry, Dan, so those players weren't,  
it wasn't a case of thinking, well, we've got a  massive game on Tuesday. We thought this might be,  
but not for what was happening on Tuesday,  but because some of them they haven't trained,  
they haven't had the opportunity to start again.  So, just with Bukayo, he's obviously had two games  
off the bench now, do you feel like he's in a  position that he could start on Tuesday? Well,  
he's in a much better place, obviously we  have built that up, he played 30 minutes,  
he's played forty-nine, a little bit less,  because we whistled before we end of the game.  
And after that, he will be in a much better  place. Can I just ask you one? Obviously,  
you got that big decision about who plays that  left centre-back without Gabriel. How did you  
feel Jakub did today? And also, is Ben moving  back to centre-back something you're thinking  
about with those games with Real Madrid? Yeah,  we have alternatives there today. Obviously,  
we had players that they haven't played  together, so that coalition hasn't been there.  
Ben especially hasn't played at all almost this  season. So good that they have demeanours, they  
have that understanding. And we will assess what's  the best options for that back line. A couple  
of here. Jordan Athletic. Can I just check how  Mateo Mario is feeling after the headlock? He's  
fine. I just checked with the doc that he  had a cut, so he was bleeding quite a lot in  
the first half, then started that game. So,  but overall he wasn't feeling anything. So,  
good. No more than any injury? No. I want to.  I obviously sent someone who doesn't play any  
part for you, you hate to do a job, but you know  you're a very much looked former Everton player  
coming back to Goodison Park for the last  time. Just off your thoughts on the sleeve,  
you say how difficult it is to come in? Well,  I mean, I think the Premier League has got a  
reputation all over the world for places like  Goodison Park. I think that makes you unique,  
the Premier League. So it's going to be very  strange. I understand this evolution of football,  
of a football club. But this is very much part of  the history of this league. And when you want to  
describe somebody from abroad, how is the Premier  League looks like, he said, go to Goodison Park  
and experience it. And unfortunately, in a few  months, we're not going to have that again. Mikel,  
Everton's gone now. How much excitement, how much  anticipation is there among your players now,  
even on the journey home about Tuesday night?  Yeah, I mean, one of the most beautiful games that  
you can play in football in the highest European  competition against the team that has dominated  
that competition in the last 20, 25 years. So,  yeah, really looking forward to it. And do you  
just rest, rest and rest now? Is that all you can  do? Oh, we have to train and prepare a few things,  
but tomorrow we'll have some time to rest and  start preparing really well the game because  
we're looking forward to the game, yeah.  Thank you. Thanks, everyone. Yeah, thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Everton 1-1 Arsenal
